findings.title: Exposure as an assigned condition
findings.claim: The absent screen can be read as one assigned environmental condition among differing ways human communities meet the sun; the focus does not turn geography into one universal protection pattern.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier نَجْعَل at 18:90:11 carries the state-changing sense of bringing an existing participant into a condition, while 18:17 supplies a contrasting solar setting in which the cave moderates the sun's path and the wider pericope supplies constructed protection as another condition.
findings.reader_payoff: The people without a screen become a situated exposure arrangement rather than an abstract absence, while the plain scene of direct sunlight remains visible.
findings.containment: This does not decide why the arrangement was made, assign a moral status to the people, or derive a single geographic policy; the literal lack of a screen remains the primary scene.

epistemic.reason: A trusted focus-anchored publication and the exact 18:17 relation ground the state contrast; the legacy walk is retained as corroborating but qualified evidence.
